should python add a switch statement.answer: PEP 3103 (A Switch/Case Statement, 2006) proposed this; it was rejected. Rejection Notice: "A quick poll during my keynote presentation at PyCon 2007 shows this proposal has no popular support. I therefore reject it." (https://peps.python.org/pep-3103/#rejection-notice). PEP 622 (Structural Pattern Matching) considered "Use dispatch dict semantics for matches" and set it aside: "Implementations for classic `switch` statement sometimes use a pre-computed hash table instead of a chained equality comparisons to gain some performance. In the context of `match` statement this is technically also possible for matches against literal patterns." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0622/#use-dispatch-dict-semantics-for-matches). Superseded by PEP 634. Closest related history (not the same idea): Discussed on discuss.python.org: ""match True" statement" (2025, 20 posts, started by Alex Salas) https://discuss.python.org/t/104063.

draft a reply to someone proposing keywo.answer:
This has come up before.

- PEP 637 ("Support for indexing with keyword arguments", 2020) proposed it; it was rejected, attributed to Python Steering Council. From the PEP: "At present keyword arguments are allowed in function calls, but not in item access. This PEP proposes that Python be extended to allow keyword arguments in item access." https://peps.python.org/pep-0637/
  The ruling: https://mail.python.org/archives/list/python-dev@python.org/thread/6TAQ2BEVSJNV4JM2RJYSSYFJUT3INGZD/
  It came up again in PEP 647 (2020, Final), whose rejected idea "Narrowing of Arbitrary Parameters" cites it: "This could involve the use of keyword indexing, as proposed in PEP 637." https://peps.python.org/pep-0647/#narrowing-of-arbitrary-parameters
  It came up again in PEP 696 (2022, Final), whose rejected idea "Allowing the Type Parameters Defaults to Be Passed to type.__new__'s **kwargs" cites it: "Ideally, if PEP 637 wasn't rejected, the following would be acceptable: T = TypeVar("T")" https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/#allowing-the-type-parameters-defaults-to-be-passed-to-type-new-s-kwargs

- PEP 472 ("Support for indexing with keyword arguments", 2014) proposed it; it was rejected, attributed to Guido van Rossum. From the PEP: "This PEP proposes an extension of the indexing operation to support keyword arguments. Notations in the form `a[K=3,R=2]` would become legal syntax. For future-proofing considerations, `a[1:2, K=3, R=4]` are considered and may be allowed as well, depending on the choice for implementation." https://peps.python.org/pep-0472/
  The ruling: https://mail.python.org/pipermail/python-dev/2019-March/156693.html

A new proposal would need to answer the reasons above. People who know this history: Joseph Martinot-Lagarde, Stefano Borini, Steven D'Aprano.

why does python have vectorcall.answer: PEP 590 (Vectorcall: a fast calling protocol for CPython) is Final, written by Mark Shannon, Jeroen Demeyer. Its Motivation: "The choice of a calling convention impacts the performance and flexibility of code on either side of the call. Often there is tension between performance and flexibility." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0590/#motivation). It builds on PEP 579, PEP 573. Earlier, never-adopted proposals in its lineage: PEP 580 (Rejected), PEP 576 (Withdrawn). It set aside the approaches of PEP 580 and PEP 576 under "PEP 576 and PEP 580": "Both PEP 576 and PEP 580 are designed to enable 3rd party objects to be both expressive and performant (on a par with CPython objects)." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0590/#pep-576-and-pep-580).

was there a pep for none-aware operators.answer: PEP 505 (None-aware operators, 2015) proposed this; it was deferred, never decided. It came up again in PEP 824 (2026, Draft), whose rejected idea "Add ??= as AugAssign" cites it: "PEP 505 also suggested to add `??=` as an `AugAssign` node." https://peps.python.org/pep-0824/#add-as-augassign. PEP 823 (None-aware access operators, 2026) proposed this; it was still a draft. Discussed on discuss.python.org: "PEP 823: None-aware access operators" (2026, 87 posts, started by Marc Mueller) https://discuss.python.org/t/109159; it refers to PEP 824 (Draft), PEP 823 (Draft), PEP 505 (Deferred).

draft a reply to someone proposing a swi.answer:
This has come up before.

- PEP 3103 ("A Switch/Case Statement", 2006) proposed it; it was rejected. Its Rejection Notice: "A quick poll during my keynote presentation at PyCon 2007 shows this proposal has no popular support. I therefore reject it." https://peps.python.org/pep-3103/#rejection-notice

- PEP 622 ("Structural Pattern Matching", 2020) considered "Use dispatch dict semantics for matches" and set it aside: "Implementations for classic `switch` statement sometimes use a pre-computed hash table instead of a chained equality comparisons to gain some performance. In the context of `match` statement this is technically also possible for matches against literal patterns." https://peps.python.org/pep-0622/#use-dispatch-dict-semantics-for-matches
  PEP 622 was later superseded by PEP 634.

A new proposal would need to answer the reasons above. People who know this history: Brandt Bucher, Daniel F Moisset, Guido van Rossum, Ivan Levkivskyi.

(Drafted by Lineage from the PEP graph. Check the links before posting.)

why does python have the walrus operator.answer: PEP 572 (Assignment Expressions) is Final, written by Tim Peters, Guido van Rossum, Chris Angelico; it was accepted (attributed to Guido van Rossum). Its Rationale: "Naming the result of an expression is an important part of programming, allowing a descriptive name to be used in place of a longer expression, and permitting reuse. Currently, this feature is available only in statement form, making it unavailable in list comprehensions and other expression contexts." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0572/#rationale). Earlier, never-adopted proposals in its lineage: PEP 3150 (Deferred), PEP 359 (Withdrawn), PEP 403 (Deferred). It set aside the approach of PEP 3150 under "Alternative spellings": "See PEP 3150 for prior discussion on this subject (with the proposed keyword being `given:`)." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0572/#alternative-spellings).

was there a pep for keyword arguments in.answer: Closest related history (not the same idea): PEP 472 (Support for indexing with keyword arguments, 2014) proposed this; it was rejected (attributed to Guido van Rossum). It came up again in PEP 637 (2020, Rejected), whose rejected idea "create a new "kwslice" object" cites it: "This proposal has already been explored in "New arguments contents" P4 in PEP 472: obj[a, b:c, x=1] # calls type(obj).__getitem__(obj, a, slice(b, c), key(x=1))" https://peps.python.org/pep-0637/#create-a-new-kwslice-object; PEP 647 (2020, Final), whose rejected idea "Narrowing of Arbitrary Parameters" cites PEP 637: "This could involve the use of keyword indexing, as proposed in PEP 637." https://peps.python.org/pep-0647/#narrowing-of-arbitrary-parameters; PEP 696 (2022, Final), whose rejected idea "Allowing the Type Parameters Defaults to Be Passed to type.__new__'s **kwargs" cites PEP 637: "Ideally, if PEP 637 wasn't rejected, the following would be acceptable: T = TypeVar("T")" https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/#allowing-the-type-parameters-defaults-to-be-passed-to-type-new-s-kwargs. Closest related history (not the same idea): PEP 637 (Support for indexing with keyword arguments, 2020) proposed this; it was rejected (attributed to Python Steering Council). It had been proposed before: PEP 472 (Support for indexing with keyword arguments, 2014, Rejected). It came up again in PEP 647 (2020, Final), whose rejected idea "Narrowing of Arbitrary Parameters" cites it: "This could involve the use of keyword indexing, as proposed in PEP 637." https://peps.python.org/pep-0647/#narrowing-of-arbitrary-parameters; PEP 696 (2022, Final), whose rejected idea "Allowing the Type Parameters Defaults to Be Passed to type.__new__'s **kwargs" cites it: "Ideally, if PEP 637 wasn't rejected, the following would be acceptable: T = TypeVar("T")" https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/#allowing-the-type-parameters-defaults-to-be-passed-to-type-new-s-kwargs. Closest related history (not the same idea): PEP 736 (Shorthand syntax for keyword arguments at invocation, 2023) proposed this; it was rejected (by Python Steering Council).

has anyone proposed utf-8 string represe.answer: PEP 756 (Add PyUnicode_Export() and PyUnicode_Import() C functions) considered "Export to UTF-8" and set it aside: "CPython 3.14 has a cache to encode a string to UTF-8. It is tempting to allow exporting to UTF-8." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0756/#export-to-utf-8). Discussed on discuss.python.org: "Pre-PEP: UTF-8 String Representation" (2026, 13 posts, started by Inada Naoki) https://discuss.python.org/t/109197; it refers to PEP 393 (Final). Closest related history (not the same idea): PEP 3120 (Using UTF-8 as the default source encoding, 2007) proposed this; it was adopted.

rows.title: Proposing __parse__: a standard inverse of __str__
rows.quote: Python standardizes T → str via __str__ , but it does not for the partial inverse str ⇀ T . Given a type and a string, nothing in the standard enables introspection whether the type offers string parsing or how to invoke it. A few constructors oblige, but not all of them are useful, like bool("False") yields True .

has anyone proposed making imports priva.answer: No PEP in the graph proposed this, but it was discussed on discuss.python.org: "Making imports private by default in a future version of Python" (2026, 7 posts, started by Thomas Kehrenberg) https://discuss.python.org/t/109305. Closest related history (not the same idea): PEP 690 (Lazy Imports) considered "Making lazy imports the default behavior" and set it aside: "Making lazy imports the default/sole behavior of Python imports, instead of opt-in, would have some long-term benefits, in that library authors would (eventually) no longer need to consider the possibility of both semantics." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0690/#making-lazy-imports-the-default-behavior). It came up again in PEP 810 (2025, Final), whose rejected idea "Modification of the dict object" cites it: "The initial PEP for lazy imports (PEP 690) relied heavily on the modification of the internal dict object to support lazy imports." https://peps.python.org/pep-0810/#modification-of-the-dict-object. Closest related history (not the same idea): PEP 690 (Lazy Imports) considered "Per-module opt-in" and set it aside: "A per-module opt-in using future imports (i.e. `from __future__ import lazy_imports`) does not make sense because `__future__` imports are not feature flags, they are for transition to behaviors which will become default in the future." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0690/#per-module-opt-in). It came up again in PEP 810 (2025, Final), whose rejected idea "Modification of the dict object" cites it: "The initial PEP for lazy imports (PEP 690) relied heavily on the modification of the internal dict object to support lazy imports." https://peps.python.org/pep-0810/#modification-of-the-dict-object.

draft a reply to someone proposing null.answer:
This has come up before.

- PEP 505 ("None-aware operators", 2015) proposed it; it was deferred, never decided. From the PEP: "Several modern programming languages have so-called "`null`-coalescing" or "`null`- aware" operators, including C#, Dart, Perl, Swift, and PHP (starting in version 7). There are also stage 3 draft proposals for their addition to ECMAScript (a.k.a. JavaScript)." https://peps.python.org/pep-0505/
  It came up again in PEP 824 (2026, Draft), whose rejected idea "Add ??= as AugAssign" cites it: "PEP 505 also suggested to add `??=` as an `AugAssign` node." https://peps.python.org/pep-0824/#add-as-augassign

- It was discussed on discuss.python.org: "Add None coalescing operator in Python" (2021, 57 posts) https://discuss.python.org/t/8292. Core developers in that thread: Kumar Aditya, Pablo Galindo Salgado.

- It was discussed on discuss.python.org: "None-coalescing operator and null‑coalescing assignment" (2026, 66 posts) https://discuss.python.org/t/107510. Core developers in that thread: Paul Moore, Terry Jan Reedy.
  The thread refers to PEP 505 (None-aware operators, Deferred).

A new proposal would need to answer the reasons above. People who know this history: Mark E. Haase, Steve Dower.

tell me the history of pep 563.answer: PEP 563 (Postponed Evaluation of Annotations) is Superseded, written by Łukasz Langa; it was accepted (attributed to Guido van Rossum). Its Rationale and Goals: "PEP 3107 added support for arbitrary annotations on parts of a function definition. Just like default values, annotations are evaluated at function definition time. This creates a number of issues for the type hinting use case:" (https://peps.python.org/pep-0563/#rationale-and-goals). Resolution: "The features proposed in this PEP never became the default behaviour, and have been replaced with deferred evaluation of annotations, as proposed by PEP 649 and PEP 749." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0563/#resolution). It builds on PEP 484, PEP 526, PEP 3107, PEP 560, PEP 557, PEP 362. Earlier, never-adopted proposals in its lineage: PEP 3152 (Rejected), PEP 3124 (Deferred). It came up again in later PEPs that cite it among their rejected ideas: PEP 604 (2019, https://peps.python.org/pep-0604/#2-change-only-pep-484-type-hints-to-accept-the-syntax-type1-type2). draft a reply to someone proposing none-.answer:
This has come up before.

- PEP 505 ("None-aware operators", 2015) proposed it; it was deferred, never decided. From the PEP: "Several modern programming languages have so-called "`null`-coalescing" or "`null`- aware" operators, including C#, Dart, Perl, Swift, and PHP (starting in version 7). There are also stage 3 draft proposals for their addition to ECMAScript (a.k.a. JavaScript)." https://peps.python.org/pep-0505/
  It came up again in PEP 824 (2026, Draft), whose rejected idea "Add ??= as AugAssign" cites it: "PEP 505 also suggested to add `??=` as an `AugAssign` node." https://peps.python.org/pep-0824/#add-as-augassign

- PEP 823 ("None-aware access operators", 2026) proposed it; it was still a draft. From the PEP: "* The "`None`-aware attribute access" operator `?.` * The "`None`-aware indexing" operator `?[ ]`" https://peps.python.org/pep-0823/

- It was discussed on discuss.python.org: "PEP 823: None-aware access operators" (2026, 87 posts) https://discuss.python.org/t/109159. Core developers in that thread: Guido van Rossum.
  The thread refers to PEP 824 (None-coalescing operators, Draft).
  The thread is the discussion of PEP 823 (None-aware access operators, Draft).

A new proposal would need to answer the reasons above. People who know this history: Guido van Rossum, Marc Mueller, Mark E. Haase, Steve Dower.

- PEP 416 ("Add a frozendict builtin type", 2012) proposed it; it was rejected. Its Rejection Notice: "I'm rejecting this PEP. A number of reasons (not exhaustive):" https://peps.python.org/pep-0416/#rejection-notice
  It had been proposed before, in PEP 351 ("The freeze protocol", 2005, Rejected).

- It was discussed on discuss.python.org: "PEP 814: Add frozendict built-in type" (2025, 139 posts) https://discuss.python.org/t/104854. Core developers in that thread: Victor Stinner, Steve Dower.
  The thread is the discussion of PEP 814 (Add frozendict built-in type, Final).
  The thread refers to PEP 603 (Adding a frozenmap type to collections, Draft).

This is already part of Python through PEP 814; a change to it would start from that PEP. People who know this history: Donghee Na, Victor Stinner.

tell me the history of pep 472.answer: PEP 472 (Support for indexing with keyword arguments) is Rejected, written by Stefano Borini, Joseph Martinot-Lagarde; it was rejected (attributed to Guido van Rossum). Its Motivation: "The indexing syntax carries a strong semantic content, differentiating it from a method call: it implies referring to a subset of data. We believe this semantic association to be important, and wish to expand the strategies allowed to refer to this data." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0472/#motivation). It builds on PEP 468. It came up again in later PEPs that cite it among their rejected ideas: PEP 637 (2020, https://peps.python.org/pep-0637/#create-a-new-kwslice-object).

rows.title: Support for indexing with keyword arguments
rows.quote: This PEP proposes an extension of the indexing operation to support keyword arguments. Notations in the form `a[K=3,R=2]` would become legal syntax. For future-proofing considerations, `a[1:2, K=3, R=4]` are considered and may be allowed as well, depending on the choice for implementation.

rows.title: Proposing __parse__: a standard inverse of __str__
rows.quote: Python standardizes T → str via __str__ , but it does not for the partial inverse str ⇀ T . A few constructors oblige, but not all of them are useful, like bool("False") yields True .

tell me the history of pep 838.answer: PEP 838 (Adding python-version to pyvenv.cfg) is Draft, written by Konstantin Schütze. Its Rationale: "The `python-version` key is not yet used by any known tool (GitHub code search), avoiding breakage in tools that read any of the existing keys. (https://peps.python.org/pep-0838/#rationale).

tell me the history of pep 690.answer: PEP 690 (Lazy Imports) is Rejected, written by Germán Méndez Bravo, Carl Meyer; it was rejected by Python Steering Council. Its Rationale: "The aim of this feature is to make imports transparently lazy. "Lazy" means that the import of a module (execution of the module body and addition of the module object to `sys.modules`) should not occur until the module (or a name imported from it) is actually referenced during execution." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0690/#rationale). Earlier, never-adopted proposals in its lineage: PEP 406 (Withdrawn). It came up again in later PEPs that cite it among their rejected ideas: PEP 810 (2025, https://peps.python.org/pep-0810/#modification-of-the-dict-object).

tell me the history of pep 422.answer: PEP 422 (Simpler customisation of class creation) is Withdrawn, written by Alyssa Coghlan, Daniel Urban. PEP Withdrawal: "This proposal has been withdrawn in favour of Martin Teichmann's proposal in PEP 487, which achieves the same goals through a simpler, easier to use `__init_subclass__` hook that simply isn't invoked for the base class that defines the hook." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0422/#pep-withdrawal). It builds on PEP 3115, PEP 367, PEP 3135. It came up again in later PEPs that cite it among their rejected ideas: PEP 487 (2015, https://peps.python.org/pep-0487/#a-more-new-like-hook), PEP 520 (2016, https://peps.python.org/pep-0520/#a-namespace-keyword-arg-for-class-definition). It was later superseded by PEP 487.

tell me the history of pep 590.answer: PEP 590 (Vectorcall: a fast calling protocol for CPython) is Final, written by Mark Shannon, Jeroen Demeyer. Its Motivation: "The choice of a calling convention impacts the performance and flexibility of code on either side of the call. Often there is tension between performance and flexibility." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0590/#motivation). It builds on PEP 567, PEP 579, PEP 573, PEP 436, PEP 489. Earlier, never-adopted proposals in its lineage: PEP 580 (Rejected), PEP 576 (Withdrawn), PEP 3146 (Withdrawn), PEP 550 (Withdrawn). It set aside the approaches of PEP 580 and PEP 576 under "PEP 576 and PEP 580": "Both PEP 576 and PEP 580 are designed to enable 3rd party objects to be both expressive and performant (on a par with CPython objects)." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0590/#pep-576-and-pep-580).

tell me the history of pep 572.answer: PEP 572 (Assignment Expressions) is Final, written by Tim Peters, Guido van Rossum, Chris Angelico; it was accepted (attributed to Guido van Rossum). Its Rationale: "Naming the result of an expression is an important part of programming, allowing a descriptive name to be used in place of a longer expression, and permitting reuse. Currently, this feature is available only in statement form, making it unavailable in list comprehensions and other expression contexts." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0572/#rationale). It builds on PEP 3155. Earlier, never-adopted proposals in its lineage: PEP 3150 (Deferred), PEP 359 (Withdrawn), PEP 403 (Deferred). It set aside the approach of PEP 3150 under "Alternative spellings": "See PEP 3150 for prior discussion on this subject (with the proposed keyword being `given:`)." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0572/#alternative-spellings).

cypher: MATCH (s:Topic) WHERE s.name = toLower($s) AND s.slug IS NOT NULL RETURN 'Topic' AS kind, s.name AS key, 'topic ' + s.name AS name, s
MATCH (p:PEP {number: $n}) RETURN p.number

MATCH (p:PEP {number: $n}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:IN_TOPIC]->(t:Topic) WHERE t.slug IS NOT NULL OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:IN_COMMUNITY]->(c:Community) WHERE c.slug IS NOT NULL WITH coalesce(t, c) AS s WHERE s IS NOT NULL RETURN labels(s)[0], CASE WHEN s:Topic THEN s.name ELSE s.id END, CASE WHEN s:Topic THEN 'topic ' + s.name ELSE 'the cluster around PEP ' + toString(s.hub) END, s LIMIT 1
MATCH (q:PEP)-[:IN_COMMUNITY]->(:Community {id: $key}) RETURN q.number

MATCH (p:PEP) WHERE p.number IN $nums OPTIONAL MATCH (a:Person)-[:AUTHORED|DELEGATE_FOR]->(p) OPTIONAL MATCH (b:Person)-[:OPENED]->(:PR)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(p) WITH p, collect(DISTINCT a.name) + collect(DISTINCT b.name) AS ppl UNWIND (CASE WHEN size(ppl) = 0 THEN [null] ELSE ppl END) AS person WITH p, collect(DISTINCT person) AS people RETURN p.number, p.title, people
MATCH path = (a:Person {name: $top})-[:AUTHORED|DELEGATE_FOR]->(p:PEP) WHERE p.number IN $nums RETURN path LIMIT 6
explain: Counted distinct authors, deciders and implementers on each of 63 PEPs; 26 depend on one person
